sections.text: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च।
The intellect which does not understand what is right and what is wrong, and what should be done and what not, is under the sway of Passion.
And that which, shrouded in Ignorance, thinks wrong right, and sees everything perversely, O Arjuna, that intellect is ruled by Darkness.
The conviction and steady concentration by which the mind, the vitality and the senses are controlled - O Arjuna! They are the product of Purity.

Weve been discussing chapter 18, Moksha Sannyasa Yoga, Yoga of Liberation through Renunciation. The goal is liberation and the tool is Sannyasa. Liberation is always from some bondage, and normally we think the bondage is always imposed by someone else.
But in this case, Bhagavad Gita says the bondages are imposed by my own self. I myself have imposed these bondages on me by identifying with this material body, this material self -- the equipment which I use to transact with this world. I falsely understood it to be me.
And now all the limitations of this instrument have become my limitations. Sorrows and unhappiness are just the product of these limitations. And therefore, if I need to find ultimate happiness and ultimate liberation from sorrows and unhappiness, I need to get rid of the bondages.
So this chapter says this liberation can only come from Sannyasa. The only means available to us is Sannyasa. So then, what is Sannyasa? We learn it is Kamyanam Karmanam Nyasa.
All you have to do is simply give up the desire prompted actions. This we found is not easy. So the means again given is Tyaga.
Give up the anxiety for the fruits of actions and over a period of time you will develop Sannyasa. Once you give up the anxiety of the fruits of action, work in this world and you will develop that understanding of who you are and you will overcome the limitations that you have. That basically what we understood in the gist of the entire Bhagavad Gita.
So now this chapter summarizing our endeavor, pursuing this path of Tyaga and then ultimately getting Sannyasa, examining all the qualities that we have acquired by just associating with this Prakriti. We have this long history of associating with this Prakriti. All this time the only thing I could associate with is my material nature.
Therefore all the qualities of the Prakriti became my qualities. And we have learnt in Vedanta that this Prakriti has three basic Gunas, Satvarajas and Tamas. So everything associated with me is tainted by these three gunas.
My goal is to go beyond these three gunas and liberate myself from this identification of this Prakriti. So therefore, we have examined what makes me attached to this work. And the first thing came the Gnana.
The knowledge that the Prakriti exists and Im aware of it, makes me identify with it. Its like somebody says, why are you climbing this mountain? If I did not know it is there, I would never have any need to climb that mountain. But because it is there, I have to now climb it.
Because Im aware of the Prakriti, I identify with that recruitment because Im aware of the world of my liking. I identify with the world which I like. Also Im aware of the world of my dislike.
And again, I identify with that world for avoiding it. So my entire pursuit in life becomes pursuing that which I like and avoid that which I dont like. In all cases, what is common is my knowledge about that field of activity.
The first thing you need to say, what is the Gnana? The Gnana, what you consider Gnana at this time is of the Prakriti. Therefore it falls into these three categories of Sattvik, Rajasic and Tamasic. Just as the nature of the Prakruti has these three gunas, so weve seen the knowledge is also Sattvic, Rajasik and Tamasic.
Then he said, now the next person involved in this action is the Karta. One who considers that I exist and I do things. He said, that person again is tainted by the three gunas of the Prakriti because of the identification of the Prakriti.
So the Karta can be Sattvic, Rajasic, or Tamasic. Now you put the two together. Knowledge and I as the doer both have tendencies which are Sattvic, Rajasic, or Tamasic. The final product which comes out -- actions -- will also be Sattvic, Rajasic, or Tamasic.
All these we are evaluating and understanding so that we can introspect and see where we fall in this category, where our actions fall. Because one thing we have learned is that the gradual progression is from Tamasic to Rajasic to Sattvic. Once I have purified my mind and intellect, the only obligation I have as the seeker of the truth is to purify my internal instrument, Antakarana, my mind and intellect.
Once mind and intellect is pure, the knowledge will shine through by itself, there will be no effort required. Therefore, we keep hearing the term praptasyaprapti. This knowledge which Im seeking about myself is already available to me.
Its already with me. Im just not seeing it because Im so engrossed in the knowledge of this world that Im completely oblivious about the knowledge about myself. Once I get rid of this knowledge which is falsely coloring my personality as Sattvic, Rajasic, or Tamasic, the true knowledge will shine through.
To know this and to negate the qualities which are binding, gradually rise from Tamasic to Rajasic to Sattvic. Once I reach that sattvic tendencies and my mind and intellect are purified, the knowledge will shine through. If this room is dark, my key is in this room.
Only thing I require is turn the lights on. It will be very easy for me to find where my keys are. So Bhagawan said that this knowledge is within yourself.
You already have it and therefore nothing new you will find. There is no new accomplishments to be made. There is no new achievements to be achieved.
But finding your own self would be like finding the keys in your pocket and becoming aware of it. Therefore, the word is realization. All I am doing is becoming realized about my own self.
So if you examine Gnana Karta, Karma, then Bhagwancha Buddhi, which is a guiding factor. I see the objects or the field of actions in this world, then knowledge takes place. Mind decide whether it is like or unlikable.
Finding guidance from the intellect, then intellect will tell you how to act in this world. So therefore Buddhi is to be evaluated as whether it is Sattvik, Rajasik or Tamasik. So we have looked at the Buddhi also.
Now all of that is only useful if Im consistently pursuing my path of evolution from Tamasic to Rajasic to Sattvik. Because anything if I do once in a while is of not great value. Something which I do consistently, then it will have positive effect for me to become an expert in anything, I have to continuously work in that field.
Once in a while I do something, it becomes hobby. Thats why Im not so good. But somebody who does it consistently, he becomes good at it.
So Bhagavan said Dhruti is a very important factor in becoming successful and getting rid of unhappiness and sorrows -- the limitations of this body and intellect, the bondages. To get rid of them and to work consistently -- that consistency is what we have seen as Dhruti. And Dhruti can also be classified into three types.
Each one of us who is seeking happiness is consistently trying to be happy. See, its not that nobody will be blamed for not trying to be happy. So if you ask anybody in this world, no matter what his position is, what his caste is, what his creed is, whats the goal of your life? Have you ever tried to be happy? And the answer is, of course Im trying.
Every day, every minute of my life, Im trying to be happy. Im very consistent in finding my happiness. But how many of us are successful? The statistics are not so good.
The Bhagawan says, thats because this dhruti with which youre finding your happiness also comes in three varieties. Drutya, Yaya, Dharayate Manah, Prana, Indriya, Kriya Yogena or Vyabicharynya Dhruti Sapartha Satviki., and many commentators believe that Dhruti is very loosely translated in English language. Because the essence of the word Dhruti cannot be translated without understanding it.
Dhruti is fortitude -- in other words, grit, an inner strength, a force from my inner personality which will not let me give up. The things which I consider are important to me. Im trying to achieve something.
We know this world will throw some obstacles in my path. It will all dependent on how strong I am in pursuing my goal. When I encounter great difficulties, Ill evaluate my situation.
My Buddhi will say, I dont think its worth it. We will weigh the pros and cons of this situation and say, what are my risk and reward here? Depending on what I come up with, I say, well, its not worth pursuing it. Or Ill say, well, risk is not that great.
Reward may be great, lets pursue it. Prabhagawan said, thats Buddhi. Beyond this Buddhi, there is an inner strength which no matter what the circumstances are, will make me pursue my path.
Bhagawan says that dhruti. He said that dhruti also can be of three types. The first one is Dhruti, which by the power of yoga will control my manah, Pranaha and Indriyaha.
That inner force which by the power of yoga. Because I had been pursuing this path and I have seen the glimpse of my own self, I know that all the things which I associate with this Prakriti is temporary. And therefore it will allow me to control my mind, my vital functions and my senses.
We know how the world of actions works. Senses go out and get the information about the objects in this world. Mind decides whether it wants to pursue it or not.
Intellect will guide the mind whether it is worth performing that action or not. My tendency will override whatever my Buddhi will tell me to do. The Bhagavan says that force from my inner self which will let me control my mind.
I control the mind, I control my senses. It also control my intellect. So Bhagavan said that Dhrutti which allows me to control my mind, vital functions and senses is Satvik Dhruti.
Im firmly established in what is the truth. And therefore it is allowing me to pursue my path to stay connected with my truth is the Satvik Dhruti. Next one is Yayatu Dharma Kama, Artha Dharayate, Arjunah, Prasangayana, Falakangsi, Dhruti, Sapaarta Rajasi.
This one we can relate to very easily. The Bhagavanta Dhrutti which is allowing me to pursue my Dharma, Artha and Kama by Prasangena by attachment. Attachment to my Dharma, attachment to my Kama and attachment of Artha Falakaan. Because I want to get something out of it.
I am pursuing my Dharma as whatever you put it, as an architect, as a father. Because I want results out of that. So Im firmly pursuing my path of being an architect.
I want to continue practicing it. Why I want something out of it. Im attached to my Dharma.
Most people, if you take their profession away from them, they feel completely lost. They dont know who they are. But once it went, I am pursuing my path of Dharma Orthayanaka.
The four goals of life we have learned in our scriptures, Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha. The waiting vow is also. There are four steps you take will do things which is in line with my Dharma.
Whatever my Swadharma, whatever is my duties, Ill follow them. I will only be able to sustain my Dharma if I have enough wealth. Narayana also sustained this world by the power of Lakshmi.
Take the Lakshmi away from Narayana. Narayana cannot sustain this world. So if I want Artha -- acquiring wealth -- and Kama -- I want to fulfill my desires.
These three Im consistently pursuing my life driven by Prasanga and Falakangshi. Because Im attached to this three. And I want to get results out of them.
And the Bhagavan leaves out moksha because typically we are not really interested in moksha simply because I think the happiness will be in pursuing these three.

These verses complete the classification of buddhi and introduce dhriti (fortitude). Rajasic buddhi imperfectly understands dharma and adharma, what should be done and avoided (verse 31) - it has some discrimination but inconsistently applied. Tamasic buddhi, shrouded in darkness, mistakes adharma for dharma and sees everything in reverse (verse 32). This is perhaps the most dangerous state - not ignorance that knows itself as ignorance, but ignorance that believes itself to be knowledge. When wrong seems right and right seems wrong, one is deeply lost. Verse 33 introduces sattvic dhriti - the unwavering steadfastness that maintains control over mind, prana, and senses through yoga. Dhriti is more than willpower; it is the inner force that keeps one on the path despite obstacles. Dhriti cannot be adequately translated - it combines fortitude, grit, persistence, and inner strength. This quality enables one to continue when the intellect calculates that the effort is not worth it. Beyond rational assessment lies dhriti, which says this is my path, and I will walk it. Reflect on your own dhriti: When obstacles arise, what keeps you going? Is it stubbornness (tamasic), desire for results (rajasic), or genuine commitment to the path regardless of outcomes (sattvic)? Today, identify one area where your resolve has weakened. Rather than forcing yourself through willpower alone, connect with the deeper why - the yoga that naturally sustains effort. Sattvic dhriti does not come from gritting your teeth but from being established in truth. When your path aligns with your deepest nature, persistence becomes effortless.
